AGENTS.md.content:
# mini-py - for agents

> **This document owns:** the commands as the manifests name them, the conventions an agent cannot infer from the code of mini-py, and the gotchas. Forty lines at most; the README links here for the commands and the docs index owns everything else. *(draft, review me)* - the commands are read from the manifests; conventions and gotchas are open questions

## Commands

- install: `pip install -e .` [pyproject.toml]

## Conventions

- open question: what an agent gets wrong here without being told (the branch, commit and PR rules are CONTRIBUTING's)

## Gotchas

- open question: the precondition that costs an afternoon here

## Docs

- [docs/INDEX.md](docs/INDEX.md) - the map; read it before the folder.

docs/INDEX.md.content:
# mini-py docs

> A small Python service fixture. Deliberately has no docs folder.

> **This document owns:** the map of every doc in this repository - one line each with what it owns and its state.

Pick the one file you need here; do not read the folder. Every doc says what it owns under its title; a fact has one home and the other docs link to it. State is one of `skeleton`, `draft`, `unreviewed`, `reviewed YYYY-MM-DD`, `none YYYY-MM-DD` (a person confirmed the doc says nothing applies here, so there is nothing to read), `stale YYYY-MM-DD`. A doc whose own marker says `auto` was reshaped by the tool and is listed as `unreviewed`.

## Getting started

- [Setup](getting-started/SETUP.md): the path from a clean machine to a first visible success - prerequisites, install, run, what success looks like, and what to do when it fails. Existing text to fold in: README.md § Getting started. - skeleton
- [Onboarding](getting-started/ONBOARDING.md): the reading order for a new person, the path per role, and the vocabulary this repository uses. - skeleton

## Guides

- [Development](guides/DEVELOPMENT.md): the daily loop of changing code here - run, debug, lint, test. How a change gets in (branch, commit, PR, review) is CONTRIBUTING's. - skeleton
- [Deployment](guides/DEPLOYMENT.md): how this is deployed - every deployable unit, its environment, the steps, and how to roll back. - skeleton
- [Operations](guides/OPERATIONS.md): how this is run in production - health checks, alerts, what to do when each one fires, and who is on call. - skeleton
- [Testing](guides/TESTING.md): how this repository is tested — the runners, where tests live, how to run them, and what CI checks. - skeleton
- [Contributing](guides/CONTRIBUTING.md): how a change gets into this repository - branch and commit rules, the pull request, review, and the licence contributions fall under. What CI runs is TESTING's. - skeleton

## Reference

- [Architecture](reference/ARCHITECTURE.md): the map of the system - its context, the containers it runs as, the building blocks inside them, how a request moves at runtime, how it is deployed, and the qualities and risks that shaped it. - skeleton
- [Configuration](reference/CONFIGURATION.md): every environment variable and flag this repository reads - its name, which unit reads it, whether it is required, and where its example lives. Names only, never a value. - skeleton
- [Data model](reference/DATA_MODEL.md): where data lives and what it means - the stores, the entities and their relationships, the conventions, and the migrations. - skeleton
- [API reference](reference/API.md): the endpoints — path, method, auth, request and response shape, errors. The API is the contract; nobody reimplements it. - skeleton
- [CLI reference](reference/CLI.md): the commands this repository exposes — each command, its arguments and flags, and what it does. - skeleton
- [Integrations](reference/INTEGRATIONS.md): every third party this repository talks to - what it is for, which unit calls it, and what breaks when it is down. The environment names are CONFIGURATION's. - skeleton
- [Security](reference/SECURITY.md): how a caller proves who it is, what a role may do, how secrets are handled, which data is sensitive, and the gaps known today. - skeleton

## Explanation

- [Product](explanation/PRODUCT.md): what the product is, who it is for, the idea it hangs on, how success is measured, its principles, and what it has said no to. - skeleton

## Start here

Four files, in this order. Everything else is one hop from the second one.

1. **This file** - what mini-py is and how the repository is laid out.
2. **[docs/INDEX.md](docs/INDEX.md)** - the index of every doc: what each one owns and its state. Pick the one file you need there; do not read the folder.
3. **[AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md)** - the commands as the manifests name them, and the conventions a coding agent or a new contributor needs; forty lines at most.
4. **[docs/getting-started/ONBOARDING.md](docs/getting-started/ONBOARDING.md)** - what to read next, in which order and per role (a skeleton today).

Until the fourth is written, the first stops: [the commands](AGENTS.md#commands). The index says which file is which; this README keeps no list of its own, so the two cannot drift.
<!-- /docs-structure: start here -->

readme_append.content:
## What it is

*Three sentences at most: what it does, for whom, and the one idea it hangs on. The long form is PRODUCT's; link it.*
readme_append.heading: What it is

readme_append.content:
## Quickstart

*Numbered: a link to SETUP § Prerequisites, then install, run, the URL or command that proves it works. For an application the install and run commands are a checked copy of AGENTS.md § Commands; for a library or CLI they are the consumer's install and first call, a checked copy of PUBLIC_API § Install and import or CLI § Install and invoke (when neither doc exists, AGENTS.md's install and run) - the one place a command is repeated, so a reader can start without a hop (R11 diffs the copy against its owner). SETUP owns the full path; this is the sixty-second version.*
readme_append.heading: Quickstart

readme_append.content:
## Repository layout

*A table, one row per top-level folder or unit: folder, what lives there, its own README when it has one. From the tree, never invented.*
readme_append.heading: Repository layout

readme_append.content:
## Commands

*One line and a link to AGENTS.md § Commands, which owns every command with its source. Never a second table here: a command with two homes drifts.*
readme_append.heading: Commands

readme_append.content:
## Configuration

*One line and a link to CONFIGURATION.md (or the example env file). Never an environment table here: names have one home.*
readme_append.heading: Configuration

readme_append.content:
## Status

*The file and field that hold the version (never the value, which changes every release), the licence file by name (none: say so), the CI workflow by name. One line each.*
readme_append.heading: Status
